resources.string: OpenCineCam needs camera access to show the viewfinder and capture local media.
A capability-honest cinematic camera built with public Android APIs.
Local only · no accounts · no cloud · no telemetry

Show framing guides over the preview. They are never recorded.
Show a roll indicator with inclination. Requires a gravity or accelerometer sensor.
Tap-to-focus stays enabled; this also meters automatic exposure around the selected point.

Microphone permission is required to meter and record audio.
The hardware did not initialize a compatible audio route.
De-squeeze an adapter lens in the preview and output file.
Compatible bakes orientation into the pixels. Native raster keeps sensor dimensions and writes an MP4 rotation matrix.
Choose a tactile dial or an adaptive button grid.
Let the viewfinder use the whole screen and float the controls over it.
Fit shows the whole frame; Fill covers the screen and crops the edges.
Monitoring only: transform OCLog2/BT.2020 to Rec.709. It is never baked into the recording.
Where 18% grey lands in OCLog2. The HLG source places it about 1.9 stops lower than the SDR (high frame rate) source.
Each source keeps its own curve. No gain is applied.
SDR clips are scaled down to the HLG grey. Lossless: nothing clips.
HLG clips are scaled up to the SDR grey. Highlights above about 75% HLG signal clip.

Visible recording status and stop action
Manual presets clamp pinch/rocker to each lens sector. Automatic lets the camera switch lenses as you zoom.
Freeze current focus or perform a focus scan before locking.
Recording: light and monitoring apply now. Format and audio changes are saved for the next take.

Display session active; content not visible
Self recording moves this interface and can turn off the inner screen. Start it between takes. Closing a display session does not stop recording.
The close policy applies to the next take. Hinge detection is active; recording remains subject to system camera availability.
This device does not report a hinge-angle sensor. Automatic stop on closing is unavailable; stop explicitly.
Separate preview and controls at the hinge
The operator has not loaded a script.
Hinge sensor availability has not been checked yet.
Preview is available in Video and LOG. Exterior mirror and view assist do not change the recorded image. A display session starts only when you request it.
Camera preview requires Video or LOG mode.
Preview paused — last frame is out of date
Operator viewfinder disconnected; capture processing continues.
The timer applies only to the transferred self-recording role. Zero starts immediately. Tap capture again to cancel; returning, changing camera or losing preview cancels it.
Countdown cancelled: camera state changed or the deadline expired.
Manual supplies ISO and shutter together. Native priorities keep the other parameter automatic only when advertised. Angle follows capture FPS, not project FPS.
Professional controls are unavailable on this constrained HFR route pending qualification.
Requested mode unavailable on this camera/profile. The current request uses AUTO; the preference is retained.
Requested time: %1$s ns · planned: %2$s ns · reported: %3$s ns · reported ISO: %4$s
The request is limited by the sensor range or capture frame duration. Check reported values.
HAL antibanding affects AE. The separate 50/60 Hz shutter suggestions select 1/100 or 1/120 s; they do not guarantee removal of PWM flicker.
Reported exposure mode: %1$s · reported HAL antibanding: %2$s
This WB request is adapted to the current camera: unsupported CCT/preset uses AUTO; unsupported tint uses 0.
Return exposure and WB to AUTO
Professional control update rejected; previous request retained: %1$s
Some requested controls are unavailable here; check Exposure settings.
Independent camera image controls, not audio effects. Defaults restore the capture-request template. RAW may bypass these processing stages. Verify reported values and the resulting image.
Saved for after this take. Processing is frozen during video preparation, recording and finalization.
Constrained HFR uses template defaults pending processing qualification.

OIS and EIS are selected separately; simultaneous support is not inferred. EIS can crop or change the field of view. Actual operation depends on resolution, FPS and output surfaces; check reported results, not only advertised modes.
A requested mode is not advertised here. The corresponding template value is retained; the preference is preserved.
This camera advertises processing session parameters. Changes between takes may cause a HAL reconfiguration delay; new sessions receive the requested parameters up front.
Reported image noise mode: %1$s · reported edge mode: %2$s
Reported sensor crop [left, top, right, bottom]: %1$s. This does not measure every EIS crop.
Submitted request: OIS=%1$s, EIS=%2$s · noise=%3$s · edge=%4$s. This is not the hardware result.

Continuous keeps live controls. Hold waits for AUTO convergence and a confirmed camera lock before creating the clip (up to 3 seconds); presets and Kelvin keep their fixed setting. Finalization restores the selected preview WB. Buffered GPU frames older than the confirmed lock are excluded.
AUTO lock is not advertised here, or this is constrained HFR. Hold will not start an unconfirmed take; choose Continuous explicitly or a supported fixed WB in a regular session.
Policy changes apply to the next take. WB changes during a held take remain pending until finalization.
Preparing WB · waiting for camera confirmation…
WB was not confirmed. No clip was started. Retry, or choose Continuous in Settings.
WB preparation cancelled · no clip started

Save complete portable settings, capture mode, focus intent and zoom. Input device IDs, teleprompter script/cue and calibrated lens marks stay local. C1/C2 open a review, never start recording. Up to 32 presets; JSON imports up to 64 KiB.
During preparation, REC and finalization, structural settings, mode, focus and zoom wait for the next take. Qualified live settings may change now.
The saved library could not be read. Its data has not been replaced. Restore a backup or explicitly reset the library.
This saves the preset in the library; it does not apply it. Updating replaces its settings with the current requested configuration.

Compare requested settings below. The current lens is retained. Unsupported values may be clamped or remain unavailable; an unavailable capture mode stays unchanged. Review hardware-reported values after applying. Scripts and audio device routing stay local.
Only the name changes; the saved settings remain intact.
Three buttons share Settings. Volume keys act once per press, only in the focused capture screen; dialogs and Settings keep system volume. Preset actions always open a review.

Applied once when the capture service starts, not when folding or reopening a window. Unsupported last modes use Photo. No automatic capture, lens selection, manual focus or zoom restoration. Turning restoration off resets those saved values at startup.
Lock capture controls during a take
Capture controls locked. Stop, cancel, monitoring and Settings remain available.

Locks exposure, WB, light, focus and zoom from preparation through finalization. Settings edits stay pending; turn this switch off to unlock. Presets cannot unlock a take. Monitoring and stop/cancel remain available.
Action unavailable for this camera, role or take. Check Settings.
unavailable: scopes paused because the device is too hot
Paused while the device is too hot. It comes back by itself once the device cools down; recording is not affected.
Scopes paused: device is too hot
Thermal load %1$s. Risk of a thermal shutdown: %2$s
Hold a button to read what it does.
Unassigned. Map an action to this button in Settings \u203a Operator.
Leaves the key to the system volume; it cannot be mapped to an on-screen button.
Starts a take, stops the running one, or cancels a pending capture.
Turns the torch on or off. Unavailable on high-speed profiles and on cameras without a torch.
Steps to the next torch intensity and wraps to the lowest. Needs a camera with an adjustable torch.
Outlines the in-focus edges over the viewfinder. Monitoring only: it never reaches the recorded file.
Stripes the areas above the exposure threshold. Monitoring only: it never reaches the recorded file.
Shows the tonal distribution of the frame. Monitoring only: it never reaches the recorded file.
Draws the luma levels across the frame, left to right, so clipped highlights and crushed shadows show at a glance. Monitoring only: it never reaches the recorded file.
Draws the colour of the frame around a hue circle, to check saturation and skin tones. Monitoring only: it never reaches the recorded file.

Monitors LOG as Rec.709 instead of the flat OCLog2 image. Monitoring only: the recorded file stays OCLog2. Off, the viewfinder looks washed out because that is what LOG is. Available only in LOG mode.
Drops the manual focus mark and hands focus back to the camera.
Pulls focus to mark A over the configured duration and easing.
Pulls focus to mark B over the configured duration and easing.
Opens preset C1 for review; nothing is applied until you confirm.
Opens preset C2 for review; nothing is applied until you confirm.
Opens or closes the take session on the subject screen.
Arms the lock that freezes the capture controls during a take. Stop, cancel, monitoring and Settings stay available.
Select one image per interval and encode it at the project frame rate. Silent SDR; codec availability is checked when recording starts.
Changes apply to the next take; this recording keeps its original configuration.
Sensor target: %1$d fps, independent of project rate

Off-speed applies to SDR VIDEO only: every captured image receives a project timestamp. Audio is explicitly muted, not stretched; your audio preference is preserved for normal takes. Sensor FPS stays independent and follows available camera profiles. Encoder support is checked at REC.

Silent timelapse pause keeps the viewfinder live. Resume captures an image and restarts the interval; the duration limit counts active time only. The file keeps continuous project FPS. VIDEO/LOG with calibrated embedded AAC uses a separate shared-capture pause policy.
Shared capture clocks · codec priming unverified
AAC source window applied · playback/lip sync unverified

VIDEO/LOG pause uses matching capture clocks with calibrated embedded AAC or separate WAV/FLAC. Preview and meters stay live while both saved streams omit the same source intervals. Separate files retain source-offset metadata; editor alignment is not automatic. Unknown clocks and off-speed do not advertise this route.

REC counts muxed video frames; REGEN continues after the last saved take. FREE uses the monotonic display clock, including pauses. Changes during REC apply to the next take. Metadata is saved in a JSON sidecar, not a container timecode track. Rates are independent of project rate; source synchronization is not verified.
Enter a valid label for the selected rate. Drop-frame omits frames 00/01 at most minute boundaries (00–03 at 59.94 DF).

Restores completed-take positions after reopening. Turning this off resets the next take and clears stored continuity. FREE restarts its display clock after reopening. Recovery of a take interrupted by process termination is not verified. This preference stays local, outside presets.
The next take starts at the configured initial value. A running take keeps its timecode; existing files remain unchanged.
Timecode continuity storage failed; reopening may restart the counter.
Saved locally; complete-file recovery record could not be stored.
Register complete new takes for the persistent transfer queue. Existing captures are not added automatically.
Destination address only; no password, query or fragment.
Allow cellular and metered networks for transfers
Off by default. Wi-Fi only unless cellular is enabled. Destination changes apply to new takes; previously registered destinations stay bound.
Settings were not applied. Check the HTTPS address and local settings storage.
Complete take registered in the WebDAV queue
Saved locally; WebDAV registration needs recovery
Stored only on this device using Android Keystore. They stay outside presets and the queue. Changing the destination does not copy credentials.
Credentials need recovery. Explicitly remove the stored record before saving new credentials.
Remove credentials for this destination only? Captures, destination settings and queued files remain unchanged.
Credentials were not applied. Check the entered values and device credential storage.
Choose a complete registered take to send its files and verify the remote copy. No automatic uploads or additions from capture history.
No complete registered takes to display.
Ready for an explicit send request.
Sending files. Server acknowledgement is not verification.
Reading back the remote copy for verification.
The selected take has all files verified.
Transfers are paused while recording or waiting for recording to start.
Enable WebDAV in settings before sending.
Metered or cellular transfer requires your explicit consent in settings.
The original destination needs valid credentials.
The remote file differs; no overwrite will be attempted.
The local source is unavailable or has changed.
Remote copy not verified. Verification is required before another send.
The transfer needs attention. Refresh to inspect each file.
Cancellation requested. A remote copy may already exist; check the file states.
Waiting for all files to be published
Transfer cleanup is still pending. Recording has not started.

Only for a saved endpoint with a literal private or loopback IP address. Disabling certificate verification allows server impersonation and may expose credentials and recordings. Leave this off unless you trust the local network.

Applies to PHOTO, independently of the continuous torch. Auto requires automatic exposure. Forced flash supports automatic or manual exposure; priority modes remain unavailable. The camera meters before automatic flash and restores the preview light afterward. OFF means no pulse and preserves an already requested continuous torch.
This flash/exposure combination is unavailable: %1$s. Change the selection before taking a photo.
Pulse levels require forced flash and adjustable single-flash hardware. Auto flash chooses its own intensity. Torch levels are configured separately.
Last photo — flash: %1$s · reported level: %2$s. Reported metadata does not certify physical illumination.
requested level exceeds the lens range
automatic flash controls its own strength
JPEG, a RAW + JPEG pair from one exposure, or native HEIC when this camera advertises it. RAW mode saves DNG only.
The selected format is not advertised by this camera. Choose another format; captures never silently fall back to JPEG.
Quality applies to compressed stills, not DNG. Each capture includes a relation file with its timestamp and file hashes.
Changes apply after the current capture finishes.
Separate JPEG exposures, not merged HDR. Requires automatic exposure; no photographic flash pulse. Continuous torch remains independent. Count and step must fit the advertised camera range exactly.
Select automatic exposure on a camera that supports AE before capturing a bracket.
This camera does not advertise usable exposure compensation.
The camera cannot represent this EV step exactly. Select a different step.
The entire bracket does not fit this camera. Reduce count or EV step; exposures are never silently clamped.
Cancellation or capture failure discards the unpublished sequence. Only the complete set is saved. Publication failure attempts to remove every created file; this is not crash-atomic storage.
Saved bracket metadata and separate JPEG exposures: %1$d
Cancel bracket and discard unpublished exposures

Select Light Painting capture mode. Combines sequential JPEGs in linear sRGB, with gaps between captures; not a continuous sensor exposure. Use a tripod. Automatic exposure may vary and is recorded per frame.
LIGHT: per-channel maximum retains bright light trails.
WATER: temporal mean smooths motion without accumulating brightness.
STARS: retain the brightest whole RGB pixel above the linear luminance threshold; the first frame supplies the background. No star alignment or tracking.
BULB: additive simulated integration increases brightness and clips highlights; not physical continuous Bulb exposure.
Maximum duration, ms: %1$d (finish early after two frames)
Minimum capture interval, ms: %1$d (processing may extend it)
Maximum output edge, px: %1$d; no upscaling

Only the final JPEG and its frame metadata are saved. Cancel discards the unpublished result. Processing keeps bounded buffers, not every source image. Saving uses compensated publication, not crash-atomic storage.
Saved accumulation and metadata; source frames: %1$d
Width:height of the final oriented JPEG. Center pixel crop without upscaling; not sensor readout, zoom or a viewfinder guide. Preview stays full-frame.
Use whole numbers from 1 to 10000 for both values.
JPEG, HEIC, burst, bracket and accumulation crop pixels. RAW remains intact: its relation records the request, not an applied crop.

HEIC crop decodes and re-encodes SDR sRGB8-bit pixels at the selected quality. A compatible HEIC or HEVC encoder is required. HDR, wide-gamut and arbitrary EXIF are not preserved. Unsupported encoding fails without publishing or converting to JPEG.
3–10 sequential JPEGs with shared quality and crop. Capture speed varies with processing; no fixed frame rate. Only complete sets are saved; cancellation or failure discards the unpublished set.
Interrupted photo groups discarded: %1$d; recovery pending: %2$d
Transfers wait while local media files are being changed.
Use native Surface for exact frames
Native Surface frames: exact positions require a render callback. Color follows the system pipeline; changing output restarts review without autoplay.
%1$s: this display advertises the matching HDR type. Physical HDR fidelity is not verified.
%1$s: this display does not advertise the matching HDR type. The system may tone map to SDR.
Delete the proxy video and its relation JSON listed below. The original is preserved. An interrupted deletion resumes when the app next starts.
I confirm deletion of these two derived files.
Only the proxy video filename changes. Its URI and video bytes, the original, and the relation JSON filename remain unchanged. The relation records the new proxy name.
Verified proxy files, including those retained after deleting an original. Original names are historical references; their current availability is not checked here.
You can record this take without audio or grant microphone access.
Android lets you choose the input device; it does not guarantee selecting an individual built-in microphone capsule.
AAC is embedded in the MP4. WAV and FLAC are saved as synchronized sidecars with capture metadata.
The camera did not start the preview in time.
High-speed rates (HS) record every frame; the viewfinder shows 30 fps while they run.

Exactly as the camera reports them; numbers in parentheses are the Android API constants. Tap a long value to expand it.
Resolutions and frame rates offered in Video mode.
120/240 fps capture and slow motion through constrained high-speed sessions.
LOG recording derived from the 10-bit HLG stream, or from the ISP at high frame rates.
ISO, shutter speed and shutter-angle dials in professional exposure.
EV compensation while exposure is automatic.
Flicker reduction for 50 Hz or 60 Hz mains lighting.
AE lock, which can also be held for the whole take.
Manual focus dial, focus pulls and AF lock.
Tap to focus and tap to meter exposure on the viewfinder.
Kelvin and tint white balance; without Kelvin, the camera\'s AWB presets.
AWB lock, so colour stays constant during a take.
Lens buttons on the zoom bar that jump to each physical lens.
Zooming while recording in high-speed modes.
Noise-reduction and sharpening control; Off gives a flatter image for grading.
DNG photos, alone or paired with JPEG.
Torch as a video light, with intensity levels where the camera allows them.
Photo flash modes and, where available, flash strength.
Aligns separate WAV/FLAC audio files with the video through the sensor clock.
